tools.description: Append a timestamped note to the journal, e.g. advice given to the player this session.

save_path.description: Save to identify the playthrough; omit for most recent

game_h.description: In-game hours when this happened (omit to use the save's current time)

tools.name: add_journal_entry

tools.description: Add a new objective (a goal, build order, or task) to the plan.

save_path.description: Save to identify the playthrough; omit for most recent

tags.description: Optional tags, e.g. economy, military, exploration

tools.name: add_objective

tools.description: Analyse one of the player's OWN construction plans for ratios: per-ware production vs internal consumption, which intermediates run a deficit (and how many extra modules would close it), which mined resources it needs, sellable surplus, workforce jobs vs housing, storage and build cost. This is the INVERSE of plan_production/plan_complex — those design a station from scratch, this audits one he already laid out. Use it for any 'is my station balanced / what did I get wrong / check my ratios' question.

plan.description: Construction plan name (exact, or a substring that matches exactly one). List them with list_plans.

sunlight.description: Sunlight factor of the intended sector (e.g. 1.5); scales Energy Cells output. Default 1.0

sector.description: Sector name to take the sunlight factor from instead of passing it directly

race.description: Workforce race whose diet to charge (argon/teladi/paranid/split/terran/boron). Defaults to the race of the plan's habitation modules, else the race of its food modules, else argon.

workforce.description: Workers to feed. Defaults to the OPTIMAL workforce — every job the plan's production modules offer at full staffing.

tools.name: analyze_plan

tools.description: Health-check one player station: cross-references what it PRODUCES against its live buy/sell offers and storage to flag SHORTAGES (a ware it makes but is still buying = feeder modules undersized; a raw it mines but is running low = add miners) and SURPLUSES (a raw piling up = over-mined, cut/redeploy miners; a product accumulating = downstream consumer or sales undersized). Returns current production-module counts per ware so you can decide what modules to add. Run after a build completes to see if the ratios are balanced.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

raw_low.description: Storage below this counts as 'running low' when also being bought (default 3000)

accumulating.description: A produced ware stored above this (and not being bought) = accumulating/downstream undersized (default 25000)

tools.name: diagnose_station

tools.description: What a ship ACTUALLY costs fitted, not the bare hull price. Reads the hull's real equipment slots (L/M turrets, weapons, shields, engines) from the install and prices them, because equipment is usually most of the bill — a Behemoth E hull is 9.25M and the fitted ship is ~26M. Returns a min/avg/max band (component prices float with the economy) plus a total at LIVE prices from stations the player has discovered, which is the closest thing to a wharf quote. Pass turret='flak' to price a specific loadout, quality='best' for the top of the range. Use this for any fleet budget — never quote a hull price as the cost of a warship.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

ship.description: Ship name or macro (e.g. 'Behemoth E', 'Minotaur Raider')

turret.description: Substring picking the turret type to fit, e.g. 'flak', 'plasma', 'beam'. Omit for the cheapest compatible.

quality.description: 'budget' (cheapest compatible, default) or 'best' (most expensive) — the spread between them is most of the price

race.description: Restrict components to a maker race (argon, teladi, paranid, split, terran, boron). Defaults to the hull's own race.

markup.description: Optional multiplier applied to the totals, for markups or discounts this tool cannot see. Default 1.0. Against a real Behemoth E quote the modelled max band was already within 1%, so a markup is usually NOT needed.

tools.name: estimate_ship_cost

tools.description: Rank sectors for siting a solar (Energy Cells) factory by sunlight (which scales output), annotated with local energy-cell demand, owner and gate-neighbour count. Hostile (Xenon/Kha'ak) sectors are excluded by default.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

tools.name: find_energy_sites

tools.description: Rank sectors by the abundance of a minable resource. Solids (ore, silicon, ice, nividium, scrap) are ranked by field weight; gases (hydrogen, helium, methane) are matched by presence in the sector.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

resource.description: Resource to rank by: ore, silicon, ice, nividium or scrap

tools.name: find_mining_sectors

tools.description: Aggregate the BUY demand across discovered NPC stations (optionally within a sector): which wares many stations want, total quantity, and best price. Reveals what is profitable to produce or sell. The core opportunity-finder.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

sector.description: Limit to discovered stations in sectors whose macro/name contains this substring

tools.name: find_supply_gaps

tools.description: Search the live trade offers of NPC stations the player has discovered. Filter by ware and by whether you want to BUY it (returns stations selling it, cheapest first) or SELL it (returns stations buying it, highest price first). The basis for trade routes and for pricing a future factory's product.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

ware.description: Ware id substring to match, e.g. energycells, ore, hullparts. Omit to list all offers.

player_wants.description: What you intend to do: 'buy' (find stations selling the ware, cheapest first), 'sell' (find stations buying it, best price first), or 'both' (default)

tools.name: find_trade_offers

tools.description: Look up station-building modules from the game database by macro, name substring, produced ware, or class (production/habitation/storage/dock/buildmodule/defence). Returns each module's class, size, race, produced ware + workforce it employs (production), workforce it houses (habitation), or hold capacity + cargo type (storage). This is the hardware layer that complements get_recipe (which gives the ware recipes). Module build costs are the module_* wares — use get_recipe for those.

query.description: Module macro, display-name substring, produced ware, or class (production/habitation/storage/dock/buildmodule/defence)

tools.name: get_module

tools.description: Get the persisted empire plan for a playthrough (defaults to the most recent save): overall strategy, objectives (build orders/goals) and the journal of past advice. Plans are per-playthrough and persist across save refreshes.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a .xml.gz save; omit to use the most recent save

tools.name: get_plan

tools.description: High-level snapshot of the player's empire from a savegame: credits, in-game time, faction relations, fleet/station counts and a role breakdown. Start here.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a .xml.gz save; omit to use the most recent save

tools.name: get_player_overview

tools.description: Look up a ware's production recipe and price band from the game database: inputs per cycle, cycle time, output amount, and min/avg/max price. Use to understand any commodity.

ware.description: Ware id (e.g. hullparts, energycells) or a name substring

tools.name: get_recipe

tools.description: Full detail for one player station, looked up by its code (e.g. SRC-496) or id: production, current storage levels, trade offers, workforce and subordinates.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

ref.description: Station code (e.g. SRC-496) or id to look up

tools.name: get_station

tools.description: List the blueprints the player owns (production modules, build modules, ship/equipment mods). You can only BUILD modules you have a blueprint for; missing ones must be bought from faction reps (reputation-gated) or otherwise acquired. Highlights which wares you can currently produce.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

filter.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter on blueprint id (e.g. prod, dock, weapon)

tools.name: list_blueprints

tools.description: List OWNERLESS ships anywhere in the discovered galaxy that are free to claim by spacesuit — abandoned derelicts AND unclaimed X4: Timelines reward ships. Each entry gives the hull faction, size, role and the sector it sits in. Biggest hulls first (free capitals surface at the top). Optionally filter by size/role/faction/sector. Use to find free ships to grab early — especially capital derelicts and Timelines rewards.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

size.description: Size filter: XS, S, M, L or XL

role.description: Case-insensitive role substring filter, e.g. Destroyer, Racer, Miner

faction.description: Case-insensitive hull-faction substring filter, e.g. Xenon, Paranid

from_sector.description: Reference sector (name or macro) to measure gate distance from; defaults to the player's current sector

sort_by.description: Sort order: 'distance' (closest first, default) or 'size' (biggest hull first)

tools.name: list_claimable_ships

tools.description: List sectors on the galaxy map with their controlling faction and contested/player-owned status. Optionally filter by owner faction. Use to understand the discovered galaxy and territory.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

owner.description: Filter by controlling faction, e.g. argon, teladi, xenon, ownerless

tools.name: list_known_sectors

tools.description: List the player's OWN construction plans — the station layouts saved in the build menu, plus any Exported single-plan files. Use before analyze_plan to get exact names.

filter.description: Optional case-insensitive substring to match plan names

tools.name: list_plans

tools.description: List all playthroughs that have a saved plan, with their label, strategy summary and objective count. Each X4 playthrough (game guid) keeps its own independent plan.
tools.name: list_playthroughs

tools.description: List discovered X4: Foundations savegames (newest first) with path, size and modified time. Use a save's path with the other tools, or omit save_path elsewhere to default to the most recent save.
tools.name: list_saves

tools.description: List the player's ships, optionally filtered by role/size/sector. Each entry includes its current order (what it is doing), captain, location and account.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

role.description: Case-insensitive role substring filter, e.g. Miner, Trader, Fighter

size.description: Size filter: XS, S, M, L or XL

tools.name: list_ships

tools.description: List the player's stations with what they produce, workforce, storage fill and assigned subordinate count.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a .xml.gz save; omit to use the most recent save

tools.name: list_stations

tools.description: Design ONE station that supplies MANY wares at once — the multi-target form of plan_production. Use preset='wharf' or 'shipyard' for the complete shipbuilding input set (23 wares: hull construction AND the equipment a facility mounts), resolved from the installed game data so nothing is omitted. Also accepts an explicit 'wares' list. Returns the shared, vertically-integrated module ratios across every target (overlapping tiers like energy cells counted ONCE, not summed), whole-module build plan, one-off build cost, mined raws, and which module blueprints are missing. ALWAYS prefer this over calling plan_production once per ware — that route drops inputs and double-counts shared tiers.

preset.description: Shipbuilding facility whose full input set to supply: wharf (XS/S/M hulls + equipment), shipyard (L/XL hulls + equipment), ships (all hulls, no equipment), equipment (equipment only). Resolved from the installed game data, so nothing is missed.

wares.description: Explicit target ware ids or name substrings to produce, instead of (or in addition to) a preset

modules.description: Production modules per target ware (default 1). Sets the scale of the whole complex.

build_sector.description: Sector you will build in; scales the energy-cell module count by 1/sunlight

sunlight.description: Override the sunlight factor directly; ignored if build_sector resolves

save_path.description: Save to check blueprint ownership against; omit for most recent

tools.name: plan_complex

tools.description: Size a miner / hauler / trader fleet: given a throughput (units/hr of a ware to mine-deliver or move), pick the best hull and compute how many ships you need. Covers all logistics — solid/liquid miners feed production, container haulers distribute output. Chains with plan_production (feed its raw_resources_per_hour to size miners, or its output_per_hour to size distribution haulers). Cargo comes from the ship-stat DB; throughput assumes a full cargo cycle every cycle_minutes (the key knob — shorter for in-sector, longer cross-sector).

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

ware.description: The ware to mine-deliver or move (name or id) — sets cargo type + unit volume

units_per_hour.description: Target throughput in units/hr (e.g. plan_production's raw_resources_per_hour to size miners, or output_per_hour to size haulers)

ship.description: Specific hull name/macro to use; omit to auto-pick the biggest-cargo hull of the right type

cycle_minutes.description: Minutes for one full load+travel+unload cycle (default 20; shorter in-sector, longer cross-sector) — the key assumption

all_factions.description: Include rep-gated hulls (Terran/Split/Boron) when auto-picking; default false = only buyable Argon/Teladi/Paranid

tools.name: plan_fleet

tools.description: Plan an industrial complex's raw-material supply around a TARGET sector: for each resource the complex needs, find the reachable mining sectors within a few gate jumps, ranked by abundance against distance, and say whether to refine at the complex or beside the field. Give 'produces' (e.g. hullparts, claytronics) to derive the raw resources from the game's own recipes, or 'resources' to name them directly. Use this when siting a station; use find_mining_sectors when you only want the galaxy's richest fields for one resource.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

sector.description: Target sector for the complex, by name or macro (e.g. 'Avarice IV')

produces.description: Wares the complex will produce (e.g. hullparts, claytronics). Their recipes are walked down to raw minables. Omit to consider every minable.

resources.description: Raw resources to plan for, instead of deriving them from 'produces' (ore, silicon, ice, nividium, scrap, hydrogen, helium, methane)

max_hops.description: How many gate jumps out to search (default 3)

prefer.description: Ranking: 'proximity' (default) puts the CLOSEST adequate field first, which is what a fixed delivery rate actually needs; 'abundance' ranks by field size against distance, for 'where is the most of this in the region'

include_all.description: Include hostile (Xenon/Kha'ak) and contested sectors (default false)

tools.name: plan_mining_supply

tools.description: Design a factory for a target ware: given a module count, compute output/hr, per-input consumption, gross margin, and the full vertically-integrated module ratios + raw resource needs down to mined inputs. The core station-design tool.

ware.description: Target ware id (or name substring) to produce

modules.description: Number of production modules for the target ware (default 1)

build_sector.description: Sector name/macro you will build in; scales the energy-cell module count by 1/sunlight (e.g. The Reach needs far fewer EC modules)

sunlight.description: Override the sunlight factor directly (e.g. 3.67); ignored if build_sector resolves

save_path.description: Save to check blueprint ownership against; omit for most recent

tools.name: plan_production

tools.description: Size the food + medical supply for a station's workforce. Give a habitat race (argon/teladi/paranid/split/terran/boron) and either a workforce number or a list of production modules (output wares or macros) to sum the workforce from. Returns per-hour food/medical consumption (authoritative from the game's workunit data), how many food/medical production modules that needs, and how many habitats house the workers. Teladi is the tightest self-sufficient chain (food + medical share intermediates). Chain the food/medical wares into plan_production to build their upstream chains.

race.description: Habitat race whose workforce you're feeding: argon, teladi, paranid, split, terran, boron

workforce.description: Total workforce to feed; or omit and pass production_modules to derive it from module staffing

production_modules.description: Production module output wares or macros (e.g. advancedelectronics, siliconwafers, prod_gen_energycells_macro) whose max workforce is summed to size the workforce

assume.description: Consumption rate: busy (fully staffed, default) or idle

tools.name: plan_workforce

tools.description: Report where the player is in each story/plot chain (Tides of Avarice Northriver & Curs, Erlking, HQ/Boso Ta, faction & terraforming plots), read from the savegame's Mission Director cue states. For each plot: whether it's started/in-progress/complete/skipped, the current chapter, and the milestone cues with their states (complete=passed, active=running now, waiting=next objective/frontier, cancelled=skipped by a mid-story start, pending=not yet reached). Also returns 'mod_research' — the four PHQ ship-modification research projects (Engine/Shield/Weapon/Chassis) with their quest gate and status (available/in progress/delivered/unlocked) — and 'completed_research' (finished PHQ research ware ids). Use this to advise on the next plot step. Optional 'plot' substring filters to one storyline (and omits the empire-wide research fields).

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

plot.description: Optional case-insensitive substring to filter to one plot (e.g. 'northriver', 'erlking', 'curs')

tools.name: plot_progress

tools.description: Force a re-parse of a savegame, bypassing the cache. Call this after the user saves the game again so queries reflect the latest state.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a .xml.gz save; omit to use the most recent save

tools.name: refresh_save

tools.description: Gate-jump distance between two sectors (by name or macro), for logistics/route planning. Returns hops and the resolved sector names.

save_path.description: Absolute path to a save; omit for most recent

tools.name: sector_distance

tools.description: Set the free-text overall strategy/direction for the playthrough.

save_path.description: Save to identify the playthrough; omit for most recent

strategy.description: The overall strategic direction for the playthrough

tools.name: set_strategy

tools.description: Update an objective's status (todo/in_progress/done/blocked/dropped), detail or priority by id.

save_path.description: Save to identify the playthrough; omit for most recent

status.description: New status: todo, in_progress, done, blocked or dropped
